subject: Dedicated capacity headroom request — Pegasus production launch (urgent)
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@pegasus.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask for launch — Q3 production traffic

Hi Kimberly,

Quick context: Pegasus is launching a new feature the week of July 12th that will route high-volume inference for our realtime summarization product. The engineering team’s load tests show a steady-state of ~180 concurrent streams with 12k tokens/min per stream at peak (we know units are rough).

We need to finalize reserved capacity commitments and confirm any hard limits or preemption policies — we cannot tolerate unnoticed preemption on these streams. Can Redwood confirm the feasibility of a dedicated pool (US-West) for Pegasus with 8 T4-equivalent slots plus a 20% burst buffer for the first 90 days?

Attached is a short traffic profile and expected ramp (pegasus_capacity_request_20270610.pdf). We’d like to have a decision by Friday Jun 18 to keep our rollout schedule. If this requires exec approval, please escalate and loop the right folks.

Thanks — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Platform
Pegasus AI

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700

Elaine — thanks for the details and the traffic profile.

Short answer: we can support a dedicated pool but we need to align on commitment level and exact scheduling. A couple of immediate notes:
- Region: US-West has two dedicated clusters with limited unallocated headroom the week of Jul 12.
- Preemption: our Dedicated offering can be configured with soft preemption rules (notification + graceful drain) or hard-guarantee reservations — the latter requires a higher commit or a short-term borrow from burst capacity.

I’m looping Karthik (sales lead) and Marcus (capacity planning) to provide a concrete proposal — Marcus, can you look at the attached profile and respond with options (strict reservation vs. reserve+burst vs. staged ramp) and estimated costs?

Elaine: if you can confirm absolute RTO/RPO tolerances and whether a minute-level drain is acceptable during preemption events, that will help us size the commit.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask for launch — Q3 production traffic

Kimberly / Karthik — reviewed the profile and did a quick mapping against the US-West pools. Summary of feasible options: 

Option A — Strict reservation (no preemption)
- Reserve 8 x T4-equivalent slots for Pegasus in cluster-west-2.
- Requires committing to a 3-month minimum; capacity available only if we defer two small Q3 pilots (estimated 12% of cluster).
- Tradeoff: full guarantee; higher committed cost.

Option B — Reserve+burst (recommended short-term)
- Reserve 6 slots + 20% burst buffer (auto-borrow from burst pool) for 90 days.
- Soft preemption policy: 10m notice + graceful KV eviction for affected streams. We can implement a prioritized routing tag so Pegasus falls back to pre-warmed model-variants before eviction.
- Lower commit, faster to provision, moderate risk during simultaneous peaks.

Option C — Staged ramp with hard cutover
- Start with 4 reserved slots week 1, scale to 8 over 4 weeks via scheduled capacity shifts.
- Requires close coordination with other committed customers and a rolling reassign schedule.

Important constraints: by Jul 12 we have 32% cluster utilization for reserved customers; reassigning capacity from other signed deals will require commercial approvals (discount/credits) for those customers.

I attached a working capacity plan (q3_capacity_plan_pegasus.xlsx) that models cluster utilization and suggested tranching.

If sales wants a firm guarantee for launch we’ll need exec sign-off to reprioritize the small pilots or bump to a larger commit.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Capacity Planner | Redwood Inference

Team / Elaine — thanks Marcus for the options. Quick commercial framing from my side:

- Pegasus is an attractive mid-market logo with clear expansion potential; preserving the launch timeline is high priority for GTM.
- I recommend we offer Option B (Reserve+burst) as the default with an explicit SLA addendum that defines the soft preemption window, advance notice, and an incident credit scheme if an unplanned preemption causes >X% error-rate impact. The SLA draft is attached (sla-draft-pegasus-v1.pdf).
- If Pegasus requires Option A (no preemption), we should propose a 6-month commitment at a discounted committed rate to compensate other customers that would be displaced.

Requesting approval to:
1) Offer Option B to Pegasus today and begin provisioning for a 6/28 soft-provisioning date.
2) If Pegasus signs for hard reservation (Option A), escalate to leadership for a one-off reassign of two Q3 pilot slots and sign a 6-month commit with a 15% discount.

Kimberly: please confirm with Pegasus whether Option B is acceptable so we can begin infra work.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Elaine Park <elaine@pegasus.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dan Hsu <dan.hsu@pegasus.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -07:00

Kimberly / Karthik / Marcus — appreciate the fast analysis. Option B is acceptable as a starting point, BUT: our engineers cannot tolerate any unexpected stream interruptions during the first 3 weeks of launch — even a 10 minute drain would be visible to customers and brand damaging.

We are willing to sign a short-term increased commit (6 months) if Redwood can guarantee no hard preemption for the first 30 days post-cutover. If that guarantee requires reprioritizing two pilot customers, please escalate to your leadership; we would expect a commercial concession to compensate them.

Please escalate — we need a firm green light or a short list of tradeoffs by EOD Friday Jun 18.

Best,
Elaine Park
Head of Platform | Pegasus AI
